lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé has no email address or phone number in the body.
items.because: A recruiter needs a direct way to contact you from the document.

items.says: The extracted consistency fields for unsupported skills and misspellings are empty or malformed.
items.because: They do not provide usable résumé content and may cause a parser to misread the application.

items.says: Three lines could not be placed cleanly by the parser.
items.because: Another system may lose or display content out of order.

items.says: The eight-month gap between the B.A. and the Operations Analyst role is unexplained.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what happened between June 2018 and March 2019.

items.says: EDUCATION appears before EXPERIENCE.
items.because: The review says four years of professional experience should establish the career direction first.

items.says: Harbor Payments should appear before Crestline Logistics within EXPERIENCE.
items.because: The review says the older operations role gets priority over the more recent, product-relevant internship.

items.says: The 35% checkout-conversion improvement lacks a baseline, comparison period, and type of percentage change.
items.because: A reader cannot judge its size or credibility without knowing what it was measured against.

items.says: The dispute self-service bullet does not show what changed after launch.
items.because: Shipping early and naming success metrics do not establish that the feature succeeded.

items.says: The open-ticket queue reduction lacks a starting size or precise period.
items.because: The reader cannot judge the scale of the reduction or pace of resolution.

items.says: Comparing opt-in with non-opt-in merchants cannot by itself measure the redesign's effect.
items.because: Selection bias and confounding mean a raw comparison cannot isolate its impact.

items.says: The measurement bullet gives neither the metric compared nor its result.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what changed.

items.says: The standalone onboarding measurement should sit with the onboarding result or be removed.
items.because: It repeats that story without reporting its result.

items.says: The onboarding redesign and 2,300-merchant result conflict with their attribution to the earlier practicum.
items.because: Both entries cannot place the same intervention in their stated timeframes.

items.says: The Harbor Payments internship lacks one clear product story across its separate workstreams.
items.because: Moving among checkout, disputes, chargebacks, tickets, and onboarding makes the contribution harder to scan.

items.says: Excluding weather-delayed shipments does not demonstrate a reduction in total late deliveries.
items.because: Changing the measured population can lower the reported rate without improving performance.

items.says: “Cut warehouse pick errors 30%” is missing “by.”
items.because: A percentage reduction requires that construction.

items.says: The 30% pick-error reduction lacks a comparable measurement basis.
items.because: Without an error definition, periods, or comparable denominators, the reader cannot judge the result.

items.says: “Coordinated ... and prepares” mixes past and present tense.
items.because: The role ended in 2023, so the present tense makes the timeline inconsistent.

items.says: The S&OP review and forecast-pack work has no stated outcome.
items.because: The reader cannot see what the recurring process enabled or changed.

items.says: “S&OP” is unexplained jargon.
items.because: Readers outside operations may not understand the meeting type.

items.says: The 1,800 driver-hours-a-year saving is unsupported by rollout and training alone.
items.because: The figure needs a baseline, calculation, adoption evidence, and attribution.

items.says: The claim that all 9 tonnes would have been thrown away is an unsupported counterfactual.
items.because: Pickup totals alone do not establish that the food would otherwise have been discarded.

items.says: The launch bullet does not show how the Product Lead enabled the app launch.
items.because: It omits the product decision, launch mechanism, or feature ownership.

items.says: The bullet does not establish that the volunteer system caused the drop in staff cover shifts.
items.because: Other changes may explain the before-and-after figures, and no comparison period is identified.

items.says: The time unit is repeated as “each week ... a week.”
The weekly sessions have no resulting change, recommendation, or deliverable.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what the sessions produced.

items.says: “Working sessions” is generic.
items.because: It makes the activity sound less substantive than it may have been.

items.says: The bullet does not establish that front-desk staff adopted the changes.
items.because: Designing the change does not demonstrate verified usage at four clinics.

items.says: The shortened form has no stated size or outcome.
items.because: The reader cannot gauge the intervention's impact.

items.says: Merchant onboarding is misplaced under the hospital-network practicum.
items.because: It is unrelated to the surrounding scheduling and patient-intake work.

items.says: The 2,300-merchant onboarding achievement duplicates the Harbor Payments result.
items.because: Repeating it in both entries makes ownership unclear.

items.says: Reducing time to first payment from 9 days to 4 is not exactly halving it.
items.because: Four days is a reduction of about 55.6%, not 50%.
